Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \

git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

scalar-compatibility data a dimension count needs and no more.

The statement asks for a bijection `i` of scalars `κ(e) → k`, an additive
equivalence `j` from the tangent space `Dual_{κ(e)}(m_e/m_e²)` at the identity
of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` to the two-chart Čech cokernel `Ȟ¹(S, 𝒪_C)`, and the
intertwining law `j (r • x) = i r • j x`. Given those,

`finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` — so the former "linearity
bookkeeping" leg (step 2 of the old reduction) is discharged and this is the
whole residue.

*not* determine `finrank`, and the older reduction knew that, which is why it
listed semilinearity as a separate obligation. Bundling the equivalence with its
compatibility square is precisely the strength required — no more, since `i` is
asked only to be bijective, and no less, since dropping `hc` would make the

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivFunctorDef
9	
10	/-!
11	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme (A.2.c)
12	
13	This file is the **A.2.c** assembly chapter for the project's positive-genus
14	arm of `nonempty_jacobianWitness`. It states the FGA representability of the
15	relative Picard functor of a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
16	`C/k`, following Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained
17	Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
18	
19	## Status (run-0008 rewire — `picSharp` is now the REAL relative functor)
20	
21	The former §0 placeholder (`picSharp` as a `Classical.choice` extraction from
22	a `⟨sorry⟩`-backed `Nonempty` typeclass, with **no defining property**) has
23	been replaced: `picSharp C` is now **defined** as the honest relative Picard
24	functor
25	
26	```
27	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
28	```
29	
30	on the `H_T`-coset carrier `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of sibling
31	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (§4b there; blueprint
32	`def:rel_pic_sharp` after the coordinated repin). Consequently the
33	representability statements below have actual mathematical content: the
34	`RepresentableBy` witness extracted from `representable C` is a genuine
35	natural bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is
36	what the downstream tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`,
37	`Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
38	
39	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (route (b))
40	
41	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
42	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
43	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
44	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
45	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
46	
47	```
48	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
49	```
50	
51	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
52	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
53	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
54	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is NOT
55	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
56	the representability sorry `instHasPicScheme` below is **conditional on
57	`[HasRationalPoint C]`**: an unconditional instance would assert a false
58	statement. (Run-0008 memory `I-0061`: the same trap ruled out wiring
59	`picSharp` to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.)
60	
61	## Sorry accounting after the rewires (run 0008 `picSharp`, run 0010 fga-div,
62	run 0011 Abel map)
63	
64	The file has exactly **one** remaining sorry site, a `⟨sorry⟩` instance
65	constructor of a `Prop`-valued class:
66	
67	1. `instHasPicScheme` — the single genuine **FGA sorry**: existence of a
68	   representing scheme for `picSharp C`, **locally of finite type over `k`**,
69	   given a rational point (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) + Cor `cor:algsch`,
70	   transported through §2 Thm 2.5). Run 0010 strengthened the existential to
71	   also carry local finiteness — part (1) of the same Kleiman theorem, one
72	   existence package — absorbing the former separate
73	   `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` sorry.
74	
75	`instHasAbelMap` is now **CLOSED** (run 0011): `HasAbelMap` is repinned from a
76	`Prop`-valued `Nonempty (divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C)` gate to a data-carrying
77	class with field `abel`, and the instance supplies the **substantive** Abel map
78	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]`.
79	`abelMap` therefore acquires a genuine defining property `abelMap_app_mk`
80	(no longer an opaque `Classical.choice` of a `Nonempty`).
81	
82	Everything else is REAL or PROVED:
83	
84	* `picSharp` — REAL (run 0008), the relative Picard functor.
85	* `divFunctor` — REAL (run 0010): the relative-divisor functor
86	  `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3
87	  Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel quotient encoding); consequently
88	  `instHasDivFunctor` is **PROVED** (witness: `divFunctor C`).
89	* `instPicSharpRepresentable` — **PROVED** (`Exists.choose_spec.1`): the
90	  scheme chosen by `PicScheme` represents `picSharp C` by construction.
91	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` — **PROVED** (run 0010,
92	  `Exists.choose_spec.2`): local finiteness is the second component of the
93	  strengthened `HasPicScheme` existential.
94	* `groupSchemeStructure` — **PROVED** via `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`:
95	  Yoneda transport of the abelian-group structure of `relPresheaf`.
96	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma is kept as a
97	  theorem extracting from an explicit **use-site hypothesis class**
98	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`. The former GLOBAL `⟨sorry⟩` instance was
99	  **deleted in run 0008**: it asserted `P.IsRepresentable` for *every*
100	  presheaf morphism `α : Z ⟶ P`, which is flagrantly false. Even the
101	  theorem's hypothesis list is weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem `lm:qt` (it
102	  omits quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme `Y`, not currently
103	  expressible in Mathlib — no `QuasiProjective` vocabulary), and with the
104	  étale-local lift hypothesis a Hironaka-type free ℤ/2-action on a smooth
105	  proper 3-fold gives a smooth proper equivalence relation whose quotient
106	  sheaf is an algebraic space that is NOT a scheme. The class must
107	  therefore be supplied at the use site, where quasi-projectivity of the
108	  Abel-map slice is available.
109	
110	## References
111	
112	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.

321	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
322	
323	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
324	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
325	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
326	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
327	
328	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
329	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
330	
331	/-! ### The substantive Abel map (run-0011 closure)
332	
333	The former `⟨sorry⟩`-backed `Nonempty (divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C)` carrier is
334	replaced by the **explicit** natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`, and the
335	class `HasAbelMap` is repinned to **carry the map itself** (a data field
336	`abel`, no longer a bare `Prop`), so that `abelMap` acquires a genuine defining
337	property (`abelMap_app_mk` below) rather than being an opaque `Classical.choice`
338	of a `Nonempty`.
339	
340	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
341	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
342	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
343	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
344	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
345	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
346	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
347	negation on the group-valued functor.
348	
349	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
350	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
351	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
352	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
353	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
354	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
355	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
356	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
357	
358	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
359	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
360	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
361	naturality rest only on the (landed) kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
362	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
363	
364	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
365	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
366	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/
367	
368	/-- Well-definedness of the ideal-class assignment `⟨F, q⟩ ↦ [ker q]` on the
369	divisor equivalence relation `DivFamily.Rel`: an equivalence `f : x.F ≅ y.F`
370	with `x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q` gives `ker x.q ≅ ker y.q` (`kernelCompMono` at the
371	iso `f.hom`), hence equal `H_T`-coset classes (`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/
372	private theorem abelKernel_welldef {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
373	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) {x y : DivFamily C.hom T.unop} (h : x.Rel y) :
374	    Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
375	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) =
376	      Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
377	        (⟨kernel y.q, y.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) := by
378	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
379	  exact Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
380	    ⟨(kernelCompMono x.q f.hom).symm ≪≫ Limits.kernelIsoOfEq hf⟩)
381	
382	/-- **Kernel commutes with base change for a divisor family** (the mathematical
383	heart of Abel-map naturality).  For a test map `g : T ⟶ T'` and a divisor family
384	`x` over `T`, the ideal of the pulled-back family is the pullback of the ideal:
385	`ker((g_C^* x).q) ≅ g_C^*(ker x.q)`.  Proof: `(pullbackAlong g.unop x).q` is
386	`triangleIso.inv ≫ g_C^*(x.q)`, so its kernel agrees with `ker(g_C^* x.q)`
387	(`kernelIsIsoComp`, precomposition by the iso `triangleIso.inv`); the
388	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
389	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
390	side hypotheses are exactly the `DivFamily` fields `epi`, quasi-coherent source,
391	`isFinitePresentation`, `flat`, `kerLocallyTrivial` over the cartesian
392	`quotBaseSquare`). -/

394	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
395	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T') (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop) :
396	    kernel ((DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop x).q) ≅
397	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).obj (kernel x.q) := by
398	  haveI hiso : IsIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q) :=
399	    Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseSquare C.hom g.unop) x.q x.epi

402	      x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
403	  exact kernelIsIsoComp

405	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf)).inv
406	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).map x.q) ≪≫
407	    (asIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q)).symm

8	/-!
9	# Universal global sections of a proper geometrically integral curve (campaign `B0`)
10	
11	This file supplies the **field of constants** substrate for the FGA Picard-scheme
12	representability campaign (`instHasPicScheme`, milestone `B0` of
13	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`).
14	
15	For a curve `C` over a field `k` that is **proper** and **geometrically integral**,
16	the ring of global sections `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is:
17	
18	* a **field** (`isField_globalSections`, Stacks `0BUG`(1); Mathlib
19	  `isField_of_universallyClosed`), because a proper morphism is universally closed
20	  and `C` is integral;
21	* **finite-dimensional** over `k` (`finiteDimensional_globalSections`; Mathlib
22	  `finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), because a proper morphism is locally of
23	  finite type — so `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a *finite field extension* of `k`.
24	
25	The sharp statement that this finite field extension is **trivial** — i.e.
26	`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` — is the content Kleiman/Milne use to build canonical divisors and
27	rigidified representatives (campaign `B1`, `B3`-corollary, `B6`, `J1`, `G3`).  Over
28	`k` it is equivalent to `k` being the *field of constants* of `C`; the one honest
29	remaining input is the degree-zero flat base change
30	`Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) ≅ k̄ ⊗_k Γ(C, 𝒪)` (which Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide at the
31	scheme level).  We isolate that input in the `Prop`-class `HasTrivialConstants`
32	and prove the `k`-algebra isomorphism `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k` from it
33	(`globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).  No global instance is supplied — the class is an
34	honest use-site gate, mirroring `IsConstantField` / `HasDedekindChart`.
35	
36	Campaign reference: milestone `B0` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
37	(Kleiman §2 uses `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` implicitly throughout the rigidification of
38	`Pic^♯`).  No blueprint node is claimed yet — the sharp `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` statement
39	is still gated (`HasTrivialConstants`), so `\leanok` would be premature.
40	-/
41	
42	universe u
43	
44	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
49	
50	/-! ## The `k`-algebra structure on the global sections `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` -/
51	
52	/-- The structural ring map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` of a `k`-curve `C`, obtained from the
53	structure morphism `C.hom : C ⟶ Spec k` on global sections, transported across
54	`Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k`. -/
55	noncomputable def constMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
56	    CommRingCat.of k ⟶ Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
57	  (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ C.hom.appTop
58	
59	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` induced by the structure morphism. -/
60	noncomputable scoped instance globalSectionsAlgebra (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
61	    Algebra k Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
62	  (constMap C).hom.toAlgebra
63	
64	lemma algebraMap_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
65	    algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤) = (constMap C).hom := rfl
66	
67	/-! ## `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite field extension of `k` -/
68	
69	/-- `C` proper + geometrically integral over the one-point base `Spec k` is an
70	integral scheme. -/
71	instance isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyIntegral (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
72	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : IsIntegral C.left := by
73	  haveI : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
74	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
75	  haveI : IsIntegral (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
76	    haveI : IsDomain ↑(CommRingCat.of k) := inferInstanceAs (IsDomain k)
77	    inferInstance
78	  exact GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton C.hom
79	
80	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a field.**  For a proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`,
81	the ring of global sections is a field (Stacks `0BUG`; Mathlib
82	`isField_of_universallyClosed`, valid because proper ⟹ universally closed and `C`
83	is integral). -/
84	theorem isField_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
85	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
86	    IsField Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
87	  isField_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
88	
89	/-- The structure map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is module-finite (Mathlib
90	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`, valid because proper ⟹ locally of finite
91	type).  `constMap C = (ΓSpecIso).inv ≫ appTop` and both factors are finite (the
92	first is an isomorphism). -/
93	theorem finite_constMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
94	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
95	    (constMap C).hom.Finite := by
96	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
97	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
98	  have hbij := ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv
99	  have hiso : ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom).Finite :=
100	    RingHom.Finite.of_surjective _ hbij.2
101	  have hcomp : (constMap C).hom
102	      = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
103	    simp [constMap]
104	  rw [hcomp]; exact hf.comp hiso
105	
106	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is finite-dimensional over `k`.**  Combined with
107	`isField_globalSections`, this exhibits `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` as a *finite field extension*
108	of `k`. -/
109	theorem finiteDimensional_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
110	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
111	    Module.Finite k Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
112	  finite_constMap C
113	
114	/-! ## `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` under the field-of-constants gate -/
115	
116	/-- **Field-of-constants gate** (`B0` residual).  The structure map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)`
117	is surjective — equivalently, `k` is the field of constants of `C`.  Together with
118	`isField_globalSections` this is `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`.
119	
120	There is no global instance: the honest remaining input is degree-zero flat base
121	change `Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) ≅ k̄ ⊗_k Γ(C, 𝒪)` (with `C_{k̄}` integral by geometric
122	integrality forcing the finite extension `Γ(C, 𝒪)/k` to be both separable — from
123	geometric reducedness — and to remain a domain after `⊗ k̄` — from geometric
124	irreducibility — hence trivial).  Mathlib v4.31 supplies no scheme-level `H⁰` base
125	change, so we gate on the conclusion, as with `IsConstantField`. -/
126	class HasTrivialConstants (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Prop where
127	  surjective_constMap : Function.Surjective (constMap C).hom
128	
129	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k`.**  Under the field-of-constants gate, the finite field
130	extension `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)/k` is trivial: the structure map is a `k`-algebra
131	isomorphism.  (Injectivity is automatic — `k` is a field and `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is
132	nonzero.) -/
133	noncomputable def globalSectionsAlgEquivBase (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
134	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasTrivialConstants C] :
135	    Γ(C.left, ⊤) ≃ₐ[k] k := by

186	## Sections of fibered products
187	
188	Suppose we are given the following cartesian square:
189	```
190	Y --g-→ X
191	|       |
192	iY      iX
193	↓       |
194	T --f-→ S
195	```
196	Let `Uₛ` be an open of `S`, `Uₓ` and `Uₜ` be opens of `X` and `T` mapping into `Uₛ`.
197	There is a canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, pr₁ ⁻¹ Uₓ ∩ pr₂ ⁻¹ Uₜ)`.
198	
199	We show that this map is
200	1. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen`:
201	  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ`, and `Uₓ` are all affine.
202	2. `mono_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right`:
203	  injective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is compact, and `f` is flat.
204	3. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`:
205	  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is qcqs, and `f` is flat.
206	4. `mono_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right_of_ringHomFlat`:
207	  injective when `Uₛ` is affine, `Uₜ` is compact, `Uₓ` is qcqs, `f` is flat,
208	  and `Γ(T, Uₜ)` is flat over `Γ(S, Uₛ)` (typically true when `S = Spec k`.)
209	5. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right_of_ringHomFlat`:

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.BoundedVanishing

/-!
# Adelic Riemann–Roch — global generation above the bound

This file closes the **third** of the three gaps the vanishing lane kept apart
(`Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`, module docstring): *global generation*.  Until now
that gap was recorded as "not addressed at all"; the statements below address it, and
the docstrings there and in `Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` are updated accordingly.

## What global generation means here

`𝒪(D)` is **generated by global sections at a prime divisor `P`** exactly when some
global section attains the pole bound at `P`:

`∃ f ∈ Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)), f ≠ 0 ∧ ord_P f = -D(P)`.

Such an `f` differs from a local generator of `𝒪(D)` at `P` by a unit of the DVR
`𝒪_P`, so it generates the stalk.  This is `GeneratedAt` below.  The sharper
statement is that the *whole* residue field is reached — the evaluation map

`Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)) / Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D − P)) → κ(P)`

is not merely nonzero but **onto** (`localStepMapₖ_bijective_of_vanishing`).

## The mechanism: two vanishings, not one

The evaluation map is *always* injective — that is `localStepMapₖ_injective`, the
elementary half of node N14, and it is what makes `ℓ(D) − ℓ(D−P) ≤ [κ(P):k]`.  It is
onto exactly when that inequality is an equality, and the ledger converts the
equality into a statement about `h¹`:

`ℓ(D) − ℓ(D−P) = [κ(P):k] + h¹(D) − h¹(D−P)`.

So surjectivity follows from `h¹(D) = 0` **and** `h¹(D−P) = 0`.  This is why global
generation is *strictly* more than bounded vanishing and why the threshold moves:
`deg_k (D − P) = deg_k D − [κ(P):k]`, so to put `D − P` above the vanishing bound `b`
one needs `deg_k D ≥ b + [κ(P):k]` — the bound raised by the residue degree *at that
point*.

## The three gaps, restated

With this file the ledger of gaps reads:

1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — assembled in `BoundedVanishing.lean` from
   three named inputs (base vanishing, peel, closed ledger); the first two are jointly
   equivalent to cone-vanishing (`coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel`), so this is a
   reduction and not a discharge.
2. **Extension uniformity** — still untouched, and still not even *statable*: the
   invariants here are pinned on a chosen 2-affine cover, and
   `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` does not transport that cover to `C_κ`.
3. **Global generation** — **this file**, conditional on exactly the same inputs as
   (1) and nothing more, with the threshold shifted by the residue degree.  The
   pointwise form (`generatedAt_of_bound`) is unconditional in `P`; the *uniform*
   form (`forall_generatedAt_of_bound_of_residueDeg_le`) needs a bound `r` on residue
   degrees, which is a genuine extra hypothesis over a general `k` (residue degrees of
   closed points are unbounded over a finite field) and is `r = 1` over an
   algebraically closed base.

## Provenance

Rederived in the AJC adelic abstractions.  The sibling `AJCR` proves global generation
on the `divisorSheaf` substrate via an evaluation-map/`Serre`-twist argument; none of
those identifiers exist here.  What is reused is the *idea* that global generation is
the equality case of the section-drop bound; the mechanism above (rank–nullity against
`finrank_localStepTgt`) is the adelic form and is cheaper, since the injectivity half
is already landed as N14.

/-! ## §1. The one-point-down divisor `D − P` -/

section PointDown

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]

/-- **The coefficient of `D − P` at `P` is one less.** -/
theorem sub_pointDivisor_apply_self (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
    (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) P =
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1 := by
  rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) P =
        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P -
          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from pointDivisor P) P from Finsupp.sub_apply _ _ _,
    pointDivisor, Finsupp.single_eq_same]

/-- **`D − P` agrees with `D` off `P`.** -/
theorem sub_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne (D : X.WeilDivisor) {P Q : X.PrimeDivisor}
    (h : Q ≠ P) :
    (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) Q =
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q := by
  rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) Q =
        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q -
          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from pointDivisor P) Q from Finsupp.sub_apply _ _ _,
    pointDivisor, Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne h, sub_zero]

/-- **`D − P ≤ D`.** -/
theorem sub_pointDivisor_le (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P Q : X.PrimeDivisor) :
    (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) Q ≤
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q := by
  rcases eq_or_ne Q P with rfl | hne
  · rw [sub_pointDivisor_apply_self]; omega
  · rw [sub_pointDivisor_apply_of_ne D hne]

/-- **The one-point step hypothesis for the pair `(D − P, D)`.** -/
theorem sub_pointDivisor_step (D : X.WeilDivisor) (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
    (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P =
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D - pointDivisor P) P + 1 := by
  rw [sub_pointDivisor_apply_self]; omega

end PointDown

/-- The **relative curve** `C ⊗ Spec R` over the affine test ring `R`: the underlying
scheme of the cartesian-monoidal product of `C` and `overSpec k R` in `Over (Spec k)`. -/
noncomputable def relCurve : Scheme.{u} := (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left

lemma relCurve_def : relCurve C R = (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left := rfl

/-- The relative curve is a scheme over `Spec R` via the second projection. -/
noncomputable instance relCurve.instOver : (relCurve C R).Over (Spec (.of R)) :=
  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k R)).left

/-- The **base-changed affine two-cover** of the relative curve: the preimages of the

# Base-change instances for the curve over an extension field (gap G-D5(a))

For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` (smooth of relative dimension one, proper and
geometrically irreducible over the field `k`) and a field extension `K` of `k`
(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file installs — **as instances that fire by typeclass
resolution** — every hypothesis of the landed degree/Riemann–Roch stack
(`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Degree`) for the base-changed curve

`C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,

viewed as a `K`-scheme via the **second projection** `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This is
exactly the `Over`-instance spelling that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver`
uses (`.ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`), but keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`
spelling that the Riemann–Roch files consume, rather than on the `relCurve C K` `def`.

The single geometric input is the pullback bridge `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`

section ResidueDegree

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- The `K`-algebra structure map on the residue field `κ(x)` of a scheme over `Spec K`,
through the structure morphism: `K →+* Γ(X, ⊤) →+* 𝒪_{X,x} →+* κ(x)`. Deliberately not a
global `Algebra` instance (same overlap hazard as `Scheme.overModule`). -/
noncomputable def Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap (x : X) : K →+* X.residueField x :=
  (X.residue x).hom.comp
    (((X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom).comp (X.overAlgebraMap K ⊤))

/-- The `K`-module structure on the residue field `κ(x)`, by restriction of scalars along
`Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap`. Activate with `attribute [local instance]` where needed. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def Scheme.residueFieldOverModule (x : X) :
    Module K (X.residueField x) :=
  (X.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toModule

attribute [local instance] Scheme.residueFieldOverModule

/-- **The residue degree** `[κ(x) : K]`: the `K`-dimension of the residue field at `x`. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.residueDeg (x : X) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (X.residueField x)

section RationalSection

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- **A section retracts the structure homomorphism on stalks.** For a
scheme `X` over `Spec k` and a section `e : Spec k ⟶ X.left` of the
structure morphism, the stalk map of `e` at the closed point retracts the
structure homomorphism `k ⟶ 𝒪_{X, e(*)}`. Immediate from
`comp_eq_spec_iff` applied to `ψ = 𝟙 k`. -/
lemma stalkStructureHom_comp_stalkClosedPointTo
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    stalkStructureHom X.hom (e.base (closedPoint k)) ≫ Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e
      = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k) :=
  (comp_eq_spec_iff X.hom e (𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k))).mp (by rwa [Spec.map_id])

/-- **The image of a section is a `k`-rational point.** For a scheme `X`
over `Spec k`, a section `e : Spec k ⟶ X.left` of the structure morphism and
`x` the image of the closed point under `e`, the structure map
`k → κ(x)` to the residue field is bijective. Injectivity is automatic
(`k` is a field); for surjectivity, the retraction
`stalkStructureHom_comp_stalkClosedPointTo` descends to a field
homomorphism `φ : κ(x) → k` splitting `k → κ(x)`, and a splitting by an
injective map is forced to be an inverse: `a = algebraMap k κ(x) (φ a)`
because `φ` kills the difference. -/
theorem bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (closedPoint k) = x) :
    Function.Bijective
      (algebraMap k (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x))) := by
  subst hx
  have hretr := stalkStructureHom_comp_stalkClosedPointTo X he
  have hcomp : ∀ c : k,
      (Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e).hom
        ((stalkStructureHom X.hom (e.base (closedPoint k))).hom c) = c := fun c => by
    simpa using DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom hretr) c
  set φ := IsLocalRing.ResidueField.lift (Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo e).hom with hφdef
  have hφ : ∀ c : k,
      φ (algebraMap k
        (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk (e.base (closedPoint k)))) c) = c := by
    intro c
    rw [← residue_algebraMap, hφdef, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.lift_residue_apply]
    exact hcomp c
  constructor
  · exact (algebraMap k
      (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk (e.base (closedPoint k))))).injective
  · intro a
    refine ⟨φ a, ?_⟩
    have h0 : φ (algebraMap k
        (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk (e.base (closedPoint k)))) (φ a) - a)
          = 0 := by
      rw [map_sub, hφ, sub_self]
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (φ.injective (h0.trans (map_zero φ).symm))

open TrivSqZeroExt in
/-- **The tangent space at the image of a section.** For a scheme `X` over
`Spec k` and a section `e` of the structure morphism, the over-`Spec k`
dual-number points of `X` at `x = e(*)` form the `κ(x)`-linear dual of the
cotangent space `m_x/m_x²` — `overDualNumberAtEquivCotangentSpaceDual` with
the rationality hypothesis discharged by
`bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section`. -/
noncomputable def overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (closedPoint k) = x) :
    {g : Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X.left //
        g ≫ X.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k)))
          ∧ g.base (closedPoint (DualNumber k)) = x} ≃
      Module.Dual (ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x))

/-- The structure morphism of a scheme over `Spec k`, at the level of sections over an
open `U`: the canonical ring homomorphism `k →+* Γ(X, U)`. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.overAlgebraMap (U : X.Opens) : k →+* Γ(X, U) :=
  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫
    X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op).hom

+/-!
+# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover
+
+The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
+chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
+rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
+is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
+open TopologicalSpace Opposite
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
+
+/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
+    {K : Type u} [Field K]
+    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
+    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
+    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
+    {x : X.left}
+    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
+    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
+  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
+  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
+  have hmap :
+      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
+        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
+    ext c
+    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
+      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
+      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
+      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
+    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
+    rfl
+  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
+    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
+  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
+  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
+  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
+  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
+  rw [← hmap]
+  exact h
+
+/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
+    {k : Type u} [Field k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
+    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
+    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
+      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
+  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
+    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
+    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
+  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
+  · rfl
+
+/-! ## Image-set packaging -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
+    {k : Type u} [Field k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
+    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
+      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
+      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
+    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
+  intro x hx
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
+  rw [← hpx]
+  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry
